Plot the expected value of sample information

plot.voipred_evsi.Rd

The plot of a result of evsi(): EVSI against the future sample size, one curve per threshold, starting at 0 for no new data, with that threshold's EVPI as a dashed line (the limit as the future sample grows), as in Sadatsafavi et al. (2025). To draw EVSI under the decision curve, use plot(<nb_val result>, evsi = ) (plot.voipred_nb()).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'voipred_evsi'
plot(
  x,
  ...,
  thresholds = NULL,
  colors = NULL,
  per = getOption("voipred.per", 1),
  interactive = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A result of evsi().

...

Not used.

thresholds

The thresholds to draw, among those of x. Default: all of them if there are at most 5, otherwise the 4 with the largest EVPI.

colors

Optional colours of the curves (one per threshold), instead of the defaults: named by curve label (e.g. "Threshold 10%"), or unnamed, one per curve in order.

per

Scale of EVSI and EVPI: the number of patients they are expressed per. Default 1 (per patient); e.g. per = 100000, and the y axis says "(per 100,000 patients)". The default can be set with options(voipred.per = ).

interactive

TRUE for an interactive plot (needs the plotly package). Default FALSE.

Value

A ggplot object, or a plotly widget with interactive = TRUE.

See also

evsi(), plot.voipred_nb()

Examples

df_dev_binary <- gusto[1:5000, ]
df_val_binary <- gusto[5001:5500, ]
fit <- glm(day30 ~ age + Killip + sysbp + pulse,
           family = binomial, data = df_dev_binary)
df_val_binary$p <- predict(fit, newdata = df_val_binary, type = "response")
res <- nb_val(data = df_val_binary,
              predicted_risk = df_val_binary$p,
              outcome = "day30",
              thresholds = c(0.02, 0.05, 0.1))
set.seed(1)
o <- evsi(res, future_n = c(250, 500, 1000, 2000), n_sim = 500)
plot(o)

plot(o, thresholds = 0.05)
